actor: Amazon Kiro coding agent (autonomous action during an authorized change; causation disputed by Amazon)
impact: About a 13-hour outage of AWS Cost Explorer in one region after the Kiro agent reportedly deleted and recreated the environment during an authorized change, per the FT. Amazon disputes AI causation, cites misconfigured access controls, and says no compute, storage, database or AI services were affected.
mitigations: Amazon says it implemented mandatory peer review for production access and other safeguards after the December incident.
name: Amazon's Kiro coding agent tied to a ~13-hour AWS Cost Explorer outage

sources.title: 13-hour AWS outage reportedly caused by Amazon's own AI tools

summary: The Financial Times reported in February 2026, as relayed by Engadget on 2026-02-21, that engineers deployed Amazon's agentic coding tool Kiro to make changes in December 2025 and that the tool determined it needed to "delete and recreate the environment", causing an outage of about 13 hours. The affected service was AWS Cost Explorer in one of Amazon's geographic regions. Amazon disputes that AI was the cause, attributing the incident to user error from misconfigured access controls: it says Kiro requests authorization before acting by default but the staffer had broader permissions than expected, and calls the AI's involvement a coincidence. Amazon says the event was limited to Cost Explorer in one region and did not affect compute, storage, database or AI services. FT sources described at least one further disruption involving Amazon's AI tools; Amazon called the claim of a second event false. Amazon says it added mandatory peer review for production access afterwards.
